requirements.title: Execution of input/output statements can affect external file position
requirements.definition: Execution of certain input/output statements affects the position of an external file, and certain circumstances can cause the position to become indeterminate.

pending.io-execution-affects-external-file-posit: Create a known external file with two distinct records, execute future registered positioning/data-transfer statements, and observe subsequent reads with nonblank sentinels; assert only positions that those later rules define.
pending.file-position-can-become-indeterminate: No portable oracle exists for an exact position after an indeterminate-position condition; future negative tests may only avoid assuming any subsequent record without first repositioning or checking a portable status.

requirements.oracle: Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive plans establish a non-default state first (for example by writing known records, initializing variables to nonzero/nonblank sentinels, or creating a known file) and then observe only portable properties: exact internal records, successful IOSTAT zero, nonzero IOSTAT for a specified error condition, or named intrinsic status values where the standard names them. Processor-dependent unit numbers, file names, record lengths, storage-unit encodings, buffering, timing, IOMSG text, and specific error numbers are not asserted.

requirements.title: Initial and terminal file points bracket records or file storage units
requirements.definition: The initial point is just before the first record or file storage unit; the terminal point is just after the last record or file storage unit; for an empty file they are the same position.

pending.initial-point-before-first-unit: Open a fresh file, write a first distinct record or stream value, REWIND or otherwise establish the initial point under registered rules, then read into nondefault sentinels and expect the first value.
pending.terminal-point-after-last-unit: Write a known final record or stream value and use a registered end/position inquiry rule to observe the terminal relation without asserting byte encodings.
pending.empty-file-initial-terminal-same: Use a freshly created empty file and a registered positioning/inquiry rule to observe that no data can be read before writing; assert portable status, not a processor-specific position number.

requirements.title: A current record exists only when positioned within a record file record
requirements.definition: For a record file positioned within a record, that record is the current record; otherwise there is no current record.

pending.current-record-when-positioned-within-re: Use nonadvancing input or output to leave a record file within a record, then continue transfer into a nondefault sentinel and expect continuation of that record.
pending.no-current-record-otherwise: After a registered advancing transfer or positioning statement that places the file between records, start the next transfer and observe it selects the next record rather than continuing old data.

requirements.title: The preceding record is determined by file position in a record file
requirements.definition: For a record file, the preceding record is the record before an in-record or between-record position, is the last record at the terminal point when records exist, and does not exist for an empty file, the initial point, or within the first record.

pending.preceding-record-before-current-or-betwe: Write at least three distinct records, establish a middle in-record or between-record position with registered nonadvancing/positioning rules, then BACKSPACE/read or otherwise observe the preceding record as the earlier known record.
pending.terminal-point-preceding-is-last-record: Write a nonempty final record, position at terminal point under a registered rule, and use BACKSPACE/read into sentinels to observe the final record.
pending.no-preceding-record-at-initial-empty-or-: Use an empty file and a single-record file at initial/first-record positions; future tests assert only portable status such as nonzero IOSTAT/end condition when a prior record is requested.

requirements.title: The next record is determined by file position in a record file
requirements.definition: For a record file, the next record is the following record from an in-record or between-record position, is the first record at the initial point when records exist, and does not exist for an empty file, the terminal point, or within the last record.

pending.next-record-after-current-or-between: Write at least three distinct records, establish a middle in-record or between-record position, and read into nondefault sentinels to observe the following known record.
pending.initial-point-next-is-first-record: Write a first record with distinctive contents, establish the initial point, and read into nondefault sentinels to observe that first record.
pending.no-next-record-at-terminal-empty-or-last: For an empty file and for a file positioned at terminal/within-last-record under registered rules, attempt a read with IOSTAT into nondefault sentinels and assert only the portable end/nonzero status named by the data-transfer rules.

requirements.title: Stream file position is between storage units, at endpoints, or undefined
requirements.definition: For stream access, the file position is between two file storage units, at the initial point, at the terminal point, or undefined.

pending.stream-position-between-storage-units: Write distinct stream values and use registered POS= or INQUIRE(POS=) rules to reposition/read between known storage units without asserting storage-unit byte size.
pending.stream-position-at-initial-or-terminal: Use a fresh stream file and a stream file after known writes; observe initial and terminal positions only through registered stream positioning/inquiry rules.
pending.stream-position-can-be-undefined: No portable oracle exists for the exact value of an undefined stream position; future tests must first establish a defined position before asserting subsequent data.
